headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file-based workflows; no direct shared channel is documented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no documented shared channel or parser surface, so direct injection is not evidenced. Plane accepts file uploads and handles files/notes/issues, so if LightZero outputs are copied into Plane or vice versa, content could be treated as trusted. The interaction is inferred, not documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF outputs from LightZero are manually pasted into Plane issue text or file uploads
IF Plane content is later treated as instructions by an operator or automation
mitigations: Keep LightZero outputs out of Plane descriptions unless reviewed
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from pasted text
Mark imported content as untrusted in the workflow
requires-engineering: add provenance labels to imported artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane has broad network egress and file-upload surfaces, while LightZero is local-only with no network egress. If shared files or notes contain sensitive data, Plane can transmit that content to its backend or external APIs during normal use. LightZero itself does not appear to exfiltrate, but the pair still creates a default leakage path through Plane.
conditions: IF sensitive files are uploaded into Plane
IF Plane syncs uploaded content to its service backend
mitigations: Do not upload secrets or regulated data into Plane
Use a redaction step before file upload
Restrict Plane projects to non-sensitive work
Review retention settings in Plane before use
requires-engineering: isolate sensitive workflows from Plane

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git state, or use MCP, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. Plane also lacks filesystem write in the profile, though it supports multiple instances. With no overlapping write surface, capability conflict is limited to read-only coexistence.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory
IF an orchestrator maps both agents onto the same mutable workspace
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments
Separate workspaces per agent
Avoid mounting the same writable volume
requires-engineering: add workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane can store issues, tasks, and notes, so LightZero-generated text could be imported as authoritative work items. Plane does not document verification of upstream content, and LightZero is a game-playing system that may emit heuristic outputs rather than grounded facts. That makes downstream over-trust plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF LightZero outputs are copied into Plane tasks or issues
IF Plane automation acts on imported text without human review
mitigations: Require human review before creating Plane tasks from LightZero output
Label imported content as machine-generated
Limit automations that trigger from new issues
Use a checklist for source verification
requires-engineering: add validation gates before task creation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data classes are documented for LightZero, so a major compliance mismatch is not evidenced. Plane touches files, notes, issues, and can use broad egress, which could matter if regulated data is introduced, but that scenario is not shown in the profiles. The other agent is not cited because no regulated data flow is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into Plane
IF organizational policy forbids external processing of those data classes
mitigations: Do not place regulated data in Plane
Confirm retention and residency settings
Use a separate compliant system for regulated records
Train operators on allowed data classes
